chunks: He said: And our teachers (Shaykhs) said:

We did not have any doubt that if something should happen to Abu Ja’far, no one will take his place, but Ja’far Ibn Ahmad Ibn Matil or his father, for he was Abu Ja’far’s confidant and was at his house mostly. It was known that towards the end of his life, Abu Ja’far did not eat any food that was not prepared at the house of Ja’far Ibn Ahmad Ibn Matil and his father, due to an incident that had occurred. His food was at the house of Ja’far and his father. Our scholars did not doubt that if something happened, the position will be handed to him. When he passed away and Abul Qasim was selected, they submitted to him and did not reject him. They were all with him and at his service just as they were with Abu Ja’far. Ja’far Ibn Ahmad Ibn Matil continued to serve Abul Qasim as his deputy until his death as he served Abu Ja’far Amari. Anyone who criticizes Abul Qasim in fact criticizes Abu Ja’far and finally criticizes the Divine Proof (Hujjah).

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: Abul Qasim, the successor to Abu Ja'far
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, a key deputy of the Imam during the Minor Occultation
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Divine Proof, referring to the Imam
key_terms.الْخُصُوصِيَّةِ: Special relationship or exclusive closeness to the Imam
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: The position of succession or deputyship
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: In his presence/service, indicating subordination or deputyship
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُتَيْلٍ: Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil, the specific deputy mentioned

ai.seo_question: Who was the primary deputy of the Imam during the Minor Occultation and how did the companions recognize his authority?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the continuity of the Minor Occultation by linking the authority of Abu al-Qasim directly to the established 'specialness' (khawass) of his predecessor, Abu Ja'far. It highlights Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil as the pivotal figure who maintained the Imam’s domestic and spiritual intimacy, thereby validating the companions' seamless transition of allegiance. The text serves as a theological defense against dissenters, equating criticism of Abu al-Qasim with criticism of the Imam himself.
